stop-sign.definition: A red, eight-sided road sign requires drivers to halt before crossing an intersection.

yield-sign.definition: A traffic sign tells drivers to slow or stop when needed. They must give approaching traffic the right of way before continuing.

speed-limit.definition: The highest speed at which motor vehicles may lawfully travel on a particular road or within a designated area, as set by signs or traffic law.

one-way.definition: Allowing traffic to move in only one direction along a road or lane.
one-way.exampleUsage: The sign shows that the street is one-way.

no-parking.definition: A rule or sign indicating that vehicles may not be parked in a particular place.
no-parking.exampleUsage: A no-parking sign was posted near the entrance.

pedestrian-crossing.definition: A specially marked part of a road provides a set place for people to cross. Paint, signs, traffic signals, or a raised surface may identify it.

school-zone.definition: A road area near a school where special traffic rules or lower speed limits may apply.
school-zone.exampleUsage: Drivers must follow the posted rules in the school zone.

construction-zone.definition: A road area where construction or maintenance work is taking place and temporary traffic rules may apply.
construction-zone.exampleUsage: The construction zone had temporary signs and barriers.

exit-sign.definition: A road sign showing where a driver can leave a highway, road, or facility.
exit-sign.exampleUsage: The exit sign pointed toward the airport road.

shoulder.definition: A narrow edge of land (usually unpaved) along the side of a road.

median.definition: Relating to or constituting the middle value of an ordered set of values (or the average of the middle two in a set with an even number of values).

curb.definition: A stock exchange in New York, previously known as the New York Curb Exchange.

sidewalk.definition: Walk consisting of a paved area for pedestrians.

crosswalk.definition: A marked place where people cross a road safely.

traffic-light.definition: The light’s current color tells drivers whether they may proceed, should use caution, or must stop.

roundabout.definition: A road junction at which traffic streams circularly around a central island.

overpass.definition: Bridge formed by the upper level of a crossing of two highways at different levels.

underpass.definition: An underground tunnel or passage enabling pedestrians to cross a road or railway.

brake.definition: To stop travelling by applying a brake.

signal.definition: An electrical or radio message that carries information.

overtake.definition: To catch up with and possibly overtake.

park.definition: A gear position that acts as a parking brake.

reverse.definition: Of the transmission gear causing backward movement in a motor vehicle.

u-turn.definition: A vehicle makes a tight turn, reverses its direction, and continues along the road it came from.

yield.definition: To move in order to make room for someone for something.

dui.definition: A pair who associate with one another.

seat-belt-law.definition: A law requiring vehicle occupants to use seat belts under specified conditions.
seat-belt-law.exampleUsage: The road-safety lesson explains the local seat-belt law.

right-of-way.definition: The legal priority to proceed first in a traffic situation, determined by road rules, signs, or signals.
right-of-way.exampleUsage: The driving handbook explains right-of-way rules.

blind-spot.definition: An area hidden from a person’s view, particularly beside and behind a vehicle where mirrors provide no clear view.

defensive-driving.definition: A safety-focused approach to driving that emphasizes awareness, anticipation of hazards, and compliance with traffic rules.
defensive-driving.exampleUsage: The road-safety course discusses defensive-driving principles.

road-rage.definition: Aggressive or violent acts committed by drivers during disputes on the road.

hit-and-run.definition: A traffic incident in which a driver involved in a collision leaves without fulfilling legal duties such as stopping or reporting.
hit-and-run.exampleUsage: The law treats hit-and-run as a serious traffic offense.

insurance-claim.definition: Describes something connected with submitting an insurance claim or reviewing and handling it.

traffic-ticket.definition: An official notice alleging a traffic-law violation and stating the legal process or penalty involved.
traffic-ticket.exampleUsage: The driver received a traffic ticket for the recorded violation.
